# Capture demo requests: HubSpot, form

**Pattern:** Lead Capture & Routing · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Form

## Overview

Starts when the form is submitted, and covers follow-ups work end to end across HubSpot, Microsoft Teams and Google Sheets.

It moves through 19 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. New Contact Form Submission
2. Stamp & Shape Contact
3. Payload Valid?
4. Record Rejected Input
5. Segment Audience
6. Step 1 — Welcome (Microsoft Teams)
7. Tag for Slow Nurture
8. Wait Before Step 2
9. Converted Already?
10. Step 2 — Value Nudge (Microsoft Teams)
11. Mark Converted — Stop Drip
12. Update Drip Status
13. Load Previous Snapshot
14. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
15. Stamp Completion Time
16. Persist Run Metadata
17. Summarize Run Stats
18. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
19. Send Summary to Microsoft Teams

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Microsoft Teams → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing follow-ups work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

New Contact Form Submission → Stamp & Shape Contact → Payload Valid? → Record Rejected Input → Segment Audience → Step 1 — Welcome (Microsoft Teams) → Tag for Slow Nurture → Wait Before Step 2 → Converted Already? → Step 2 — Value Nudge (Microsoft Teams) → Mark Converted — Stop Drip → Update Drip Status → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Microsoft Teams → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Microsoft Teams → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping HubSpot and Microsoft Teams aligned by hand for follow-ups
- Follow-ups sequences that run over days and must survive a restart before HubSpot
- Intake checked for completeness before it is stored in HubSpot, for follow-ups
- Follow-ups work where "Stamp & Shape Contact" is still a manual step before HubSpot

## You get

- Keeps HubSpot and Microsoft Teams in step for follow-ups, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed HubSpot or Microsoft Teams call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 22 nodes in this follow-ups build
- The pause before HubSpot is durable — a follow-ups run survives a restart
- Every follow-ups run leaves an audit row behind, alongside HubSpot
- Fans the same result out to Google Sheets in the same run, for follow-ups

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2 / service account; HubSpot private-app token; Microsoft OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Every step checks 'Converted Already?' before sending — a drip campaign that keeps emailing someone who already bought is the fastest way to burn trust. The Wait node's durable resume state (via `webhookId`) is what lets a multi-day wait survive an n8n restart instead of being held only in memory.

## Practice exercises

Already production-grade — deepen your understanding:

1. Add a 4th drip step with its own wait/exit-check pair.
2. Manually flip a test record's status to 'converted' mid-drip and confirm the ladder stops sending.
3. Shorten the wait durations so the full ladder runs in minutes instead of days, for testing.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**HubSpot private-app token**
HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Grant the CRM scopes you need; legacy API keys are deprecated and will not work.

**Microsoft OAuth2**
Azure Portal → App registrations → new app → add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions.
_Gotcha:_ Graph throttles with HTTP 429 — the retry setting on this node already handles it.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## ⏱ Rate limiting

Work is batched and spaced with Wait so provider quotas aren't tripped. If you hit 429s, lower the batch size or raise the wait — throughput drops, reliability rises.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your follow-ups process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- HubSpot: a private-app token carrying only the CRM scopes these nodes use — legacy API keys are deprecated and over-broad.
- Microsoft Teams: restrict the app registration to the target team; tenant-wide permission is not needed to post.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.

**Do not log**
follow-ups payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
